headline: Red Sox skid hits three games after a miserable Toronto loss
morning_brew: I watched that 2-1 loss against the Blue Jays last night, and I swear, I have seen more organized chaos at cousin Jimmy's backyard cookouts. It was one of those nights where the game felt like it was dragging through a swamp, capped off by a 16-minute delay that had me questioning if they were playing baseball or just arguing over the rulebook in a basement. We finally scratched a run across, but it felt about as earned as a participation trophy, and we are officially sliding down the standings with a three-game losing streak that feels heavier than a stalled train on the Red Line.

Sonny Gray gave us six innings of decent work, but when you only put six hits on the board and can not string anything together, you are practically asking to lose. The Blue Jays aren't exactly world-beaters, but we are making them look like the '27 Yankees with this pathetic lack of urgency. I will tell you exactly what is wrong with this team right now, because it is painfully obvious, we are playing like we are waiting for someone else to make a move, and that is not how you stay in the hunt for the Wild Card.

We have another date with Toronto tonight, and honestly, if we do not wake up the bats, I am going to need a lot more coffee than a regular Dunks run can provide. It is early August, and while the standings say we are still in the mix, this is the time of year when you either harden up or pack it in. I am choosing to believe they have one more rally in them, but they need to show me something tonight before I start thinking about what else I can do with my evenings besides watching us flounder at the plate.

news_digest.dans_take: About damn time we locked up a reliable target before the season really kicks into gear.

trend_watch.trend: Hitless in three at-bats Monday night
trend_watch.dans_take: The lineup is thin when he is not finding gaps, and that was a total disappearing act.

trend_watch.trend: Two hits and an RBI in the loss
trend_watch.dans_take: He is one of the few guys actually swinging like he wants to win, keep it up.
Nice to see him hold the line, but it is a damn shame the hitters could not return the favor.
